summary: Julius Eggeling was an Indologist who studied at Breslau and Berlin under scholars including Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1869–1875) and Professor at the University of Edinburgh (1875–1914).

Julius Euting worked in linguistics and history/archaeology, studying at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and Ernst Heinrich Meier. He served as Director of the Bibliothèque nationale et universitaire and Professor at the University of Strasbourg from 1880.
Julius Evola worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at ITI L.Da Vinci and Sapienza University of Rome (~1916–1919), and later held a post at Ahnenerbe (1943–1945).

Julius Grill was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Heidelberg, Jena, and Tübingen, completing his Ph.D. under Rudolf von Roth. He later taught at Blaubeuren and Maulbronn before serving as professor at Tübingen (1888–1913).

Indologist and linguist Julius Jolly studied at Munich, Berlin, Leipzig, and Würzburg under Martin Haug, Albrecht Weber, and Hermann Brockhaus. He held the Tagore professorship at the University of Calcutta (1882–1883) and was a professor at Würzburg (1877–1920).

Julius Jüthner studied at the German university of Prague (~1884–1888) and worked in history and archaeology. He held academic posts at the University of Fribourg (~1898–1903) and the University of Innsbruck (~1903–1937).

Julius Klaproth was a scholar of sinology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1801. He founded the Société Asiatique and held a chair at the University of Bonn (~1816–1835).
Julius Laber was an Indology scholar who studied at the universities of Freiburg, Leipzig, Berlin, and Bonn, earning his Ph.D. at Bonn in 1913 and studying under Hermann Jacobi in 1908.

Julius Leumann worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Geneva, Zurich, Leipzig, and Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann, Heinrich Hübschmann, and others. He served as teacher and later Rector (1906–1928) at Kantonsschule Frauenfeld.

Julius Lipner is a scholar of Indology, religion, and philosophy who studied under Hywel David Lewis at King's College London. He lectured at the University of Birmingham (~1973–1975) and served as Professor at the University of Cambridge (1975–2013).

Julius Mohl specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, and Chinese studies. He studied at Tübingen and under Silvestre de Sacy, Abel-Rémusat, and Eugène Burnouf in Paris. He held professorships at the University of Tübingen (1826–1834) and Collège de France (1847–1876).

Julius Müller was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Breslau, Göttingen, and Berlin. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1830–1835), the University of Marburg (~1835–1839), and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1839–1878).

Julius Pokorny, a linguist and Indologist, studied under Paul Kretschmer and Rudolf Much at the University of Vienna. He held posts at Vienna, Humboldt University of Berlin (1920–1935), the University of Munich, and docentships at Bern, Zurich, and Fribourg.
Julius Schubring studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1857–1858), the University of Bonn (~1858–1860), and the University of Göttingen (~1860–1862).

Indologist Julius Schwab earned his Ph.D. at the University of Munich (~1875–1882), studying under Martin Haug and Ernst Kuhn. He later worked at the Badische Landesbibliothek (1882) and as a librarian and custos at Freiburg University Library (1887).

Julius Wellhausen, a religious studies and history/archaeology scholar, studied at the University of Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald. He held posts at the universities of Greifswald (~1872–1882), Halle-Wittenberg (~1882–1885), Marburg (~1885–1892), and Göttingen (~1892–1913).

Julius von Negelein worked in Indology and religious studies, studying at Greifswald, Berlin, Marburg, and Königsberg (Ph.D.). He served as Privatdozent at the University of Königsberg (1899) and full professor at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (1920).

Juliusz J. Ossowski was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at the University of Königsberg under Adalbert Bezzenberger and Richard von Garbe.

Jun Fujii is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned a doctorate in literature from the University of Tokyo. He has served as a full-time lecturer (~2011–2014) and professor (2025) at Komazawa University.

Jun Takashima is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara. He held positions at Aichi Prefectural University (~1990–1994) and served as a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies in 2020.
